what: Śaiva ascetic institutions, maṭhas and sites in Karnataka that passed from Kālāmukha to Vīraśaiva hands

evidence.detail: Proposed in modern scholarship (e.g., D. N. Lorenzen's study of the Kāpālikas and Kālāmukhas) that the Kālāmukhas were absorbed into the Vīraśaiva movement; labeled scholarly metadata.
Neither Vīraśaiva account of origins mentions the Kālāmukhas; Allama's birthplace Baḷḷigāve was a known Kālāmukha centre (inscriptions; moderate confidence).

D. N. Lorenzen (1972) and others: several former Kālāmukha centres (including Śrīśaila) later appear as Vīraśaiva seats, and the Kālāmukhas vanish from records as the Vīraśaivas rise; some ascetics may have joined the new movement.

The Vīraśaiva tradition does not derive itself from the Kālāmukhas: the Pañcācārya account has five ācāryas (Reṇuka and others) emerge from liṅgas in each age and teach from the Śaiva Āgamas (Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi); the Liṅgāyata account centres on Basava and the śaraṇas at Kalyāṇa.
Caution: continuity of buildings is not continuity of doctrine; the vacana movement rejected the temple ritual that Kālāmukha priests served.
